text:
Victor Hedman, Norris winner and Conn Smythe winner, is playing about 15 minutes a night this season, a far smaller job than the one that made him one of the best defencemen of his generation. He played only 33 games last season. And yet the Lightning captain has four points in his last ten games, all of them goals, and Tampa has won the games he's scored in more often than not.

The chances behind it are real: his own expected goals are up, and so is his ice time, by 1:43 a night over that stretch. The finishing is not. Four goals on 1.2 expected means he's shooting 21%, against 2% last season, and that never lasts for a defenceman. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still sees the old Hedman in his passing: 6.4 primary shot assists per 60, 92nd percentile among defencemen. That's the part to watch. The goals will slow down; if the assists start arriving instead, the resurgence is real.
